title: Adoption of a Chromate-Free Sealant Standard for Pressurised Fuselage Joints
abstract: Replacement of the chromated sealant family used on pressurised fuselage joints by a chromate-free system, driven by the European restriction on hexavalent chromium and by the disposal cost the existing system carried at every repair.

sections.reason: The authorisation to use hexavalent chromium in the sealant family applied to pressurised joints expires within the planning horizon of the programme, and no extension was expected for a new build application. Beyond the regulatory driver, every repair using the chromated system generated controlled waste at the operator's own facility, which several customers had raised as a cost they could not pass on. A qualification programme run over three years established that the chromate-free system reaches the same joint life on aluminium lap joints provided the surface treatment is applied within a shorter window after abrasion.
sections.description: The chromated sealant used at pressurised fuselage lap joints, at the joint land and at every fastener installed wet is replaced by a chromate-free system with a shorter application window after surface preparation. The bolt ZEDE604998-69 and the sealant application bolt HE139604-23 are re-issued with the new surface treatment, the washer EN149290-27 is changed to the plain corrosion resistant grade because the earlier washer relied on the sealant for its protection, and the screw WES848069-85 is used at the bonding land. Cable ties LN455787K4 are re-specified because the earlier tie was incompatible with the new sealant. The change affects the fuselage joints in the cargo compartment zones 131 and 141 and the belly fairing zone 191, and every drawing that calls the chromated system is re-issued, of which D20301285477 and D20201115628 carry the practice text.
sections.effects: No mass change and no electrical load change. The joints are interchangeable in service: a chromate-free bead may be applied against a chromated bead already on the aircraft, and this is stated explicitly because a mixed joint will exist on every repaired aircraft for many years. Disposal classification of the removed material changes and the operator's waste handling instruction has to be revised. The application window shortens from four hours to ninety minutes after abrasion, which is a real constraint on a line repair and is called out in the standard practice.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00680 in July 2024. There is no retrofit of aircraft already built, since the sealant in place is not removed; Service Bulletin CRN-20-2003 exists only to release the practice into the operator's own repair procedures and to change the material call-out in the spares catalogue.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00680 after a three year qualification programme; the shorter application window required a change to the joining station sequence
